verdict.rationale: Harbor Compliance publishes a large, public OpenAPI v3 spec with OAuth client-credentials auth and idempotent endpoints, so a real first-party API exists, including registered-agent-deliveries endpoints. However, create, update, and delete operations require capabilities Harbor must explicitly grant, and nothing maps the UI surfaces (Entity/License/Tax/Records Manager, map, Compliance Score, Navigator AI, filings) to API endpoints. Missing for 10: an explicit UI–API parity claim, default self-serve write access, documented API coverage of each UI module, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: a public, keyless OpenAPI document for the Harbor Compliance API (OAuth-authenticated at runtime)
For server-to-server integrations. Exchange your client ID and secret at /api/v3/oauth/access_token with grant_type=client_credentials
Endpoints marked as idempotent accept an optional Idempotency-Key header
Creating, updating, and deleting resources requires additional capabilities which Harbor Compliance must explicitly grant to your account
